articleTitle: All optical AND gate based on silicon photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: All-optical logic AND gate is realized by incorporating an elliptical structure at the Y-junction of two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguides. Principle of operation of the device is based on linear optics and, hence, the device consumes very low power while having very fast response time. The proposed device works in the 1550 nm wavelength band. Additionally, the simplicity of the device structure and also the integrable size makes the device very efficacious for the realization of all-optical logic gate.

articleTitle: Dual-beam substrate integrated waveguide periodic leaky-wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A dual-beam substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) periodic leaky wave antenna (LWA) is designed and fabricated. The dual-beam operation is obtained by using leakage from the side walls of the SIW. The two beams are mirror image of each other. The feeding arrangement is simple and the antenna as a whole is easy to fabricate. A backward end fire to forward end fire scanning range of almost 74° is obtained by varying frequency from 8.5GHz to 13.3GHz. Side lobe level is better than 13dB in the specified frequency range. Measurement results match well with simulated results.

articleTitle: Power budget improvement in energy efficient long reach hybrid passive optical network
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Effective power consumption at central office (CO) in passive optical network can be reduced by sharing the central office resources to the maximum number of underutilized users. The choice of modulation format is very important to improve the power budget and to allow larger power splitting. Nonlinear effects for duobinary and NRZ modulation format are analyzed and behavior of reflected power from bidirectional fiber is compared for different launched powers. For a fixed BER, duobinary modulation format decreases the required receiver power as compared to NRZ thus improve the power budget. This power budget improvement is used to increase the splitting ratio to enable single optical line terminal (OLT) to serve more number of low load or underutilized optical networking units (ONUs) to reduce the CO resource requirement in order to give energy and cost efficient access network.

articleTitle: SPR based fiber sensor to measure refractive index of glycerol and acetone
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper we present a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) based fiber sensor for measurement of refractive index (RI) at different concentration of glycerol and acetone. The sensing head of fiber probe was fabricated by depositing aluminum (Al) on the unclad portion of multi-mode fiber (MMF). The experimental result shows the sensitivity obtained in power measurement of SPR fiber probe was -106.95 dBm/RIU and -408.90 dBm/RIU for glycerol and acetone. Due to the small size and good sensitivity low cost of our SPR based fiber sensor have many commercial and practical uses.

articleTitle: Design of microstrip interdigital bandpass filter with suppression of spurious responses for L-band wireless communication applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In the present paper, a compact L-band microstrip interdigital bandpass filter (BPF) with spurlines is designed. In the proposed microstrip interdigital BPF, spurious responses are suppressed and stopband attenuation is better than -14 dB everywhere upto 8 GHz excepting that near centre frequency of 4.87 GHz. The 3-dB bandwidth of the proposed BPF is 970 MHz (0.99 - 1.96 GHz) with a centre frequency of 1.475 GHz. The insertion loss value of the proposed BPF varies from 0.16 dB to 0.61 dB over the frequency range of 1.04 - 1.91 GHz. In the desired 3-dB passband, group delay is better than 2.8 ns. The proposed BPF is suitable for the application of satellite navigation like global positioning system carriers which are in the L band, centered at 1176.45 MHz (L5), 1227.60 MHz (L2), 1381.05 MHz (L3), and 1575.42 MHz (L1) frequencies, amateur radio and digital audio broadcasting.

articleTitle: Effect of noise on constellation diagram of 100 Gbps DP-QPSK systems under influence of different digital filters
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper a DP-QPSK modulation scheme has been used at 100 Gbps for the propagation length 500 km. To mitigate effects of Chromatic dispersion (CD) and Polarization mode dispersion (PMD), constant modulus algorithm (CMA) is used, while to compensate carrier phase estimation (CPE) a modified Viterbi-Viterbi algorithm is used by means of DSP at the receiver end. The comparison of constellation diagrams has been performed by using different digital low pass filters such as Gaussian, Bessel, Butterworth and Chebyshev filters, for order 1st to 6th. It is observed that Bessel filter 6th order is superior, while Gaussian filter 4th order gives second best performance.

Author Keywords: Dual Polarization Quadrature phase shift keying

articleTitle: Castor leaf-shaped quasi-self-complementary antenna for broadband applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation study of a castor leaf-shaped quasi-self-complementary antenna for broadband applications. The optimal design of proposed antenna provides -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of 2-12 GHz. It is fed with 50 Ω coplanar waveguide (CPW) with in-built matching circuit. The antenna provides directive radiation pattern along with average gain value of 4.36 dB and more than 80 % radiation efficiency over its operating frequency band. The input and radiation characteristics are obtained through simulation using Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software.

articleTitle: Design of circularly polarized waveguide crossed slotted array antenna at Ka band
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Present paper highlights an improvement over the use of conventional cross slot radiator in waveguide broadwall for circular polarization by using a combination of cross slot and inclined slot pair. Accordingly, a circularly polarized travelling wave slotted array antenna at Ka band (38.6GHz) of 20dB gain has been designed and verified in a nonstandard waveguide using the modified cross slot radiator.

articleTitle: Enabling ubiquitous sensing with RFID
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: There are various methods of automatic identification techniques. But among these methods Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) has become an excellent and reliable method for electronic identification, data capture, control, track, and inventory items using RF communication. Today RFID is having a very broad use but most of the time such systems are invisible or are not recognized by the users. RFID is replacing bar-code-based identification mechanisms, as communication between a reader and a tag( which form the RFID) is not limited by the requirement of “Line of sight” reading and each tag has a unique ID. RFID technology can be utilized to effectively optimize multiple business processes through the improvement, the automation or even the elimination of existing processes, and the emergence of new processes called intelligent processes or smart processes, which are automatically triggering actions or events. In the present work several RFID based systems have been designed and simulated. The first one is an automatic Home/Office network controller and the second one is an automatic weight monitoring system and so on. The energy consumption can be significantly reduced by designing a Home/Office network controller which detects non-operational electronic systems in a room (Light/Air conditioner) during a particular span of time and automatically turns off these systems thereby conserving energy. In the weight controlling mechanism the RFID based control unit automatically prevents overloading as well as under loading of vehicles in loading stations. Other applications have been described in a brief manner.

articleTitle: Crop variables estimation by adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system using bistatic scatterometer data
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The aim of present study is to estimate the crop variables by means of high performing technique like adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) using the bistatic scatterometer data. An outdoor 4×4 m2 crop bed of rice crop was prepared for performing all the experiments. The bistatic measurements were carried out over the entire growing stages of the rice crop from transplanting to ripening stage at the angular range of 200 to 700 with the steps 50 at both HH- and VV-polarizations in X-band. The ANFIS algorithm was used for the estimation of rice crop variables. The observed bistatic scattering coefficients and crop variables (biomass, leaf area index, plant height and chlorophyll content) were interpolated with the phenological stages of the rice crop. The 80% data sets were used for training while the remaining 20% were kept separately for the testing purposes. The bistatic scattering coefficients were used as the input data sets and the rice crop variables as the target data sets of fuzzy inference system for both the polarizations. The estimated values were found closer to the observed values of rice crop variables that indicate a satisfactory performance of ANFIS algorithm for estimating rice crop variables.

articleTitle: Vialess wideband bandpass filter using CRLH transmission line with semi-circular stub
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a via-less wideband bandpass filter using composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH-TL). The filter is designed with a closed rectangular ring resonator, interdigital capacitor, meander line and semicircular stub. The proposed filter is simulated and characterized using high frequency structural simulator ANSYS HFSS 14. Proposed filter can be operate in the frequency range of 4 GHz - 10.5 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 90% (fo = 7.9 GHz). In addition to this it offers a group delay of 0.22 ns in the passband.

articleTitle: Design of a compact and wideband branchline coupler using hybrid approach
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A compact and wideband branch line coupler is designed that covers all the navigation bands starting form xx GHz to yy GHz. A single-section coupler with series stubs, half-wavelength at the mid-band frequency f0, is considered to obtain the wideband operation. Moreover, a hybrid approach, using both transmission line sections and lumped elements, is used for the size reduction without compromising the wideband operation. A prototype branch line coupler is fabricated. The coupler has a fractional bandwidth of aa% at f0 = 1.385 GHz and a compact size of bbλg×ccλg, λg being the microstrip line guided wavelength at f0.

articleTitle: Dual bandpass filter using SIR for WLAN
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band microstrip band pass filter for 2.4 and 5.2 GHz WLAN applications. The proposed filter configuration consists of two parallel stepped impedance resonators altered to form small groove in the high impedance portion. Further, this structure is coupled to I/O and O/P transmission lines. A prototype model of the proposed filter is developed and characteristics of the filter are obtained in terms of S-parameters. A good agreement is seen between the simulation and measured results.

articleTitle: A twisted waveguide slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper the analysis of tilted slots, milled on both the broad walls of a twisted waveguide is presented. Based on the design a twisted waveguide slot antenna has been fabricated and measured. Simulated data show good agreement with measured data. The proposed antenna shows measured -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 24.64% (9.32-11.94 GHz) and simulated gain of 10.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of a s band multi-stub CPW Band Pass Filter for improved filter characteristics
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The design, characterization & fabrication of a uniplanar S band Coplanar Waveguide (CPW) Band Pass Filter has been described in the paper. The filter consists of open stub discontinuities, in series, which act as a resonant circuit, thereby exhibiting a band pass filter response. The paper also discusses about the gradual improvement in the frequency response and roll-off rate of the band pass filter, as the number of open stub discontinuity is increased while maintaining the compactness of the circuit.

articleTitle: Frequency reconfigurable mobile antenna with multi-band characteristics based on metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact multi-band frequency reconfigurable metamaterial (MTM) antenna has been proposed for mobiles. PIN diodes have been used to realize the switching application by controlling the bias voltage. With suitable selection of switch configuration, the proposed antenna offers frequency re-configurability by exhibiting wideband/multi-band behavior and covers various wireless standards such as GPS, GSM 1900, WCDMA, Bluetooth, LTE, Wi-Fi, WiMAX and WLAN. The radiation characteristics such as gain, radiation efficiency and patterns are consistent throughout the working bands. The proposed MTM antenna offers a compact size with dimensions of 35 × 35 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which makes it suitable for use in mobile units.

articleTitle: Microwave electronic CAD modeling of microwave photonic devices based on LW-VCSEL mixing
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Design principles as well as key characteristics simulation results of the VCSEL-based optoelectronic frequency converter using the powerful electronic CAD tool NI AWR Design Environment are presented. A comparison with previously reported modeling results for microwave-band optoelectronic frequency converter using a special optoelectronic CAD tool is highlighted.

articleTitle: Effect of feeding locations on bandwidth, gain and resonance frequency of the patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article effect of feeding location on bandwidth, gain and resonance frequency is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a triangular shape slot on the ground plane with rectangular shape radiating patch. The fabricated antenna FR4 substrate is used with dielectric constant 4.4. The dimension of the radiating patch and ground plane are 14 × 14 mm2 and 30 × 30 mm2 respectively. The proposed antenna offers three frequency bands of 2.714 – 2.95 GHz, 4.6 – 4.85 GHz and 6.07 – 6.58 GHz at 2.83 GHz, 4.72 GHz and 6.34 GHz. The maximum peak gain of 3.94 dBi (Simulated) and 4.8 dBi (measured) are achieved.

articleTitle: Rectangular microstrip antenna with cross headed dumbbell defected patch surface for improved polarization purity
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A simple and compact rectangular microstrip antenna with cross headed dumbbell defected patch surface is proposed for noteworthy suppression of cross polarized (XP) radiation, eliminating higher order orthogonal resonance without altering its dominant mode field configuration. The proposed antenna has been studied experimentally with theoretical justifications. More than 28 dB of XP radiation isolation from peak co polarized (CP) radiation is revealed.

articleTitle: Broadband CPW fed Stub loaded hexagonal slot backed hexagonal microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: To cover Wi-MAX and WLAN frequency bands, variations of coplanar waveguide fed hexagonal shape microstrip antennas backed by hexagonal slot ground plane in 3500 MHz frequency range is proposed. In the first variation of hexagonal shape microstrip antenna, an impedance bandwidth of more than 100% is obtained whereas 300 rotated variation of hexagonal shaped patch yields increased bandwidth of nearly 108%. Further increase in bandwidth is realized by adding stubs on the hexagonal shaped ground plane. Stub loaded MSAs yields bandwidth of around 114% and 118% in the two configurations.

articleTitle: A novel compact multi-band double Y-slot microstrip antenna using EBG structure
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel compact size triple-band microstrip antenna with and without fork like electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure is proposed for wireless mobile communication system. The proposed antenna consists of two simple Y-slots, integrating with compact size fork like EBG structure. The overall dimension of the proposed antenna is 20.5 × 23.5 × 1.6 mm3. The results show that the presented antenna cover three mobile bands with impedance beam width 28.72 MHz (1.48548 - 1.5142 GHz), 17.39 MHz (1.79134 - 1.80873 GHz) and 163.84 MHz (4.53034 - 4.69418 GHz) and resonant at 1.49997 GHz, 1.80003 GHz and 4.60004 GHz with return loss of -20.4248 dB, -14.7067 dB and -20.42458 dB respectively. The proposed antenna with EBG structure demonstrates improved performance in terms beam width, return loss, and radiation pattern over antenna without EBG structure. The design structure is fabricated using FR4 substrate with dielectric constant 4.4, loss tangent 0.02 and height of the substrate is 1.6 mm.

articleTitle: A wideband circularly polarized slotted rectangular dielectric resonator antenna excited with a cross-slot
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband circularly polarized slotted rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA) has been presented. Orthogonal modes have been excited by using a cross-slot of unequal lengths to show the circular polarization in slotted RDRA. The proposed antenna offers -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 18.37% (at center frequency 3.70 GHz) and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 18.37% (at center frequency 3.70 GHz) in the broadside direction (θ = 0°, Φ = 0°). It has been observed that the proposed antenna show the right hand circular polarization. The average gain and radiation efficiency is 4.08 dB and 83.23% in the broadside direction. This antenna is suitable for Wi-MAX application band (3.3-3.7 GHz).

articleTitle: Design of integrated Optic triple racetrack resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Optical filter using Optical triple racetrack resonator (OTRR) has been designed in this work using delay line signal processing approach in z-domain and Mason's gain formula. Silicon core with silica cladding having its effective refractive index as 2.379 has been used here as the constituent waveguide material. Based on Vernier principle enhanced free spectral range obtained as much as 23.22 THz. Group delay and dispersion characteristics are also determined for this architecture.

articleTitle: An Ultra wideband monopole antenna using Fractal shaped Parasitic Resonator for band notching characteristics
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper, investigates a compact single band notched Ultrawideband (UWB) monopole antenna with a modified Hilbert Fractal Parasitic Resonator. The antenna exhibits an Ultra Wide bandwidth which ranges from 2.61GHz-13.22GHz. The parasitic resonator results in band notching the frequency range between 7.89-8.83 GHz which is assigned for X-band satellite communication systems. This antenna can be used in various UWB communication systems.

articleTitle: Dual-band bandstop filter using single tri-section stepped impedance open stub
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper a dual-band bandstop filter using tri-section stepped impedance open stub configuration is presented. Transmission zero positions ( i.e stopbands ) can be controlled by tuning the impedances of the shunt tri-section stepped impedance unit and the series transmission line impedance is used to allocate the transmission poles to sharp the attenuation rate. Design equations were derived using lossless transmission line model. The simulated filter is fabricated using Roger/RT duroid 5870 substrate with thickness of 0.787mm and dielectric constant of 2.33. Good agreement between simulated and measured results is observed.

articleTitle: A dual band V-fractal antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper describes a dual band V fractal patch antenna, designed on FR-4 substrate with dielectric constant 4.4 and thickness h = 0.8 mm. The structure resonates at 2.14 GHz (2.11–2.18GHz) and 7.91GHz (7.83–8.47GHz) bands with % bandwidth 3.37 and 8.19 respectively with average gain of about 4 dB. The antenna parameters such as S11 (dB) and radiation pattern are simulated and presented.

articleTitle: Advance of fiber optic gas sensors for coal mine safety applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Coal mine combustion is major safety hazard, which is conventionally detected by monitoring characteristic gases such as CO, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, using a tubing bundle gas sampling system and gas chromatograph mess spectrometer. IR gas sensors have been developed to overcome the complexity and cumbersomeness of the GC analyzer, however, cross sensitivity among gases in the IR region affects the detection sensitivity and reliability. Fiber optic multi-gas sensors have been developed which provides advantage of real time detection, low cross sensitivity and low cost for coal mine combustion detection. We report latest development of a multi-gas sensor which has sub-ppm detection sensitivity. The sensors exhibit great potential for on site real time gas monitoring in coal mines and offer the advantage of early detection and warning of coal combustion.

articleTitle: A compact parallel coupled wideband bandpass filter with DGS and spurline
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A simple compact wideband coupled line bandpass filter using defected ground structure (DGS) and spurline is presented here. The proposed filter has a fractional bandwidth of 35% at central frequency 5 GHz. The conventional coupled line bandpass filter is miniaturized with the implementation of DGS in the proposed method. Return loss better than 20 dB and 3 dB bandwidth of 1.77 GHz is achieved. The spurline is incorporated in the microstrip feed line to suppress the higher order harmonics.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of entrance link using cascaded Radio-on-Fiber and digital Radio-on-Radio
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a cascaded Radio on Fiber and digitalized Radio on Radio entrance link for small cell mobile access. By utilizing wideband property of millimeter-wave, RF signals such as cellular, WiFi, or WiMAX can be digitalized and transferred to remote base station through digital Radio on Radio link. This paper will show the system configuration, and theoretical evaluations of the link design. A basic experiment shows some results of EVM measurements for WiMAX signals. The influence of the sampling rate and quantization level at ADC will be discussed. Moreover, delay characteristics of proposed system will be shown.

articleTitle: Graphen growth: 10B lead pencil, print paper, and femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Wide range grade of pencils were used to draw on variety of sheet of papers. Raman spectroscopy and multimeter evaluate graphite structure and resistance of the area on the drawn paper before laser irradiation. The 10B grade of lead pencil draw on silver-halide print paper, and femtosecond laser was employed to irradiate the area of various papers drown by 10B lead pencil with varied scanning speed and laser power. At optimal conditions of laser irradiation, Raman spectroscopy verified the multi-graphene on the B10 pencil drawn silver-halide print paper irradiated by femtosecond laser.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis of a dispersed clad mode to surrounding refractive index
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The sensitivity of a specific dispersed clad mode and a normal clad mode of a Long Period Grating (LPG) near Turn Around Point (TAP) to surrounding refractive index in the range of 1.3332 - 1.3348 has been studied experimentally. We could attain a sensitivity of ~2413 nm/RIU using LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, 11</sub> dispersed clad mode of a TAP-LPG with ~3dB attenuation at resonance.

articleTitle: Design of rectangular dielectric resonator antenna using glass added Barium Strontium Titanate
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A compact aperture-coupled dual segment rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (ACDS-RDRA) is described in this paper. The antenna consists of Teflon (εr = 2.1) as lower segment and liquid phase (glass) sintered Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) namely Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (εr = 27) as upper segment. 10 wt% of PbO-BaO-B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> glass was added to lower the sintering temperature from 1050 °C to 800 °C and increase the dielectric constant of BST. The input and radiation characteristics of ACDS-RDRA are investigated through simulation using Ansys HFSS software. The antenna provides the simulated input impedance bandwidth of 690 MHz (8.80 - 9.49 GHz) with a simulated peak gain of 6.63 dB at 9.1 GHz. The antenna provides broadside radiation patterns in both E-and H-planes of the antenna with fairly low cross-polarization levels in E-plane were obtained. Such RDRA can find potential applications in radar and satellite communication.

articleTitle: A novel design of PCF for supercontinuum source to detect oral cancer using OCT
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A PCF structure that is filled up with chloroform in its core, is optimized for generating broadest possible supercontinuum spectrum which centers at 1310 nm. It has been found that a chloroform filled PCF having airholes of diameter 1.5µm and cladding of pitch 1.2µm is capable producing broadest supercontinuum light at a shorter distance than as silica core PCF can do. The generated supercontinuum can be used as a light source in an optical coherence tomography(OCT) system to detect oral cancer with a resolution of 964 nm.

articleTitle: Wideband waveguide band-pass filter based on Broad Side Complementary Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper we have investigated Broad Side Complementary Split Ring Resonator (BS-CSRR) loaded waveguide wide band band-pass filter. Three identical BS-CSRRs were inserted in the transverse plane of a standard waveguide at a distance of 9.023 mm. The proposed waveguide filter has been simulated using Ansoft HFSS (version 14). The proposed filter is compact and has wide bandwidth and acceptable insertion and return loss.

articleTitle: Microwave and optical design optimatization of polymer phase modulators with over 40 GHz BW
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Design and performance optimization of phase modulators is presented by considering both microwave and optical characteristics. Performance modeling is conducted using OptiBPM for beam propagation method of optical waveguide and finite element method using HFSS for driving electrode design. The optical waveguide core realized using electro-optic (EO) polymer PMMI-CPO1 with a refractive index n1=1.63, EO coefficient reo=70 pm/V, RF dielectric constant εr1=3.15, and loss tangent tanδ1=10−3 that is embedded in a cladding polymer of NOA65 with n2=1.51, εr2=3.2 and tanδ2=2.2×10−2. A phase modulator with an input half-wave voltage of 8 V and a bandwidth of 43 GHz operating at the wavelength of 1.55 µm for RF and optical interaction length of 1.3cm.

articleTitle: A multi band absorber using band gap structures
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a multiband absorber using EBG structures to absorb radiation in the X-band for stealth applications. It can also be used in the K and Ka bands for reduction of Electromagnetic Interference. The structure was created using Genetic Algorithm and the simulation was performed on Ansoft High Frequency Surface Solver (HFSS). The results indicate that the structure has 97% absorption in the X band at 8.2 GHz and absorbs most of the radiation in the K, Ka bands. The structure also has low RCS and hence can find use in military applications.

articleTitle: Recent advances in access networks and their components technologies
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Recently developed technologies for 10G-class-PON and 40G-class-PON such as NG-PON2 in access networks are described, as well as a review of the current status. Key optical components for these systems are also presented. Further, the network evolution and technologies of metro-access networks for future mobile applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Dual-mode bandpass filter using via less substrate integrated waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Electroplating on dielectric is used to realize continuous metallic side walls of a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Thus the complexity of fabricating chain of metallic via using precise mechanical or laser drilling used in conventional SIW fabrication is avoided. To show effectiveness of the procedure, a single cavity dual-mode bandpass filter is designed and fabricated. A modified corner cut configuration, compatible with the via less fabrication technology, is used to obtain the dual-mode operation. The bandpass filter with microstrip lines as the external feed lines offers two transmission zeroes which is symmetrically placed on both sides of the passband. The filter has a fractional bandwidth of 5% at a center frequency 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Optical heterodyning in microwave photonic receiver for radar applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Microwave photonic receiver for radar applications comprising a continuous wave laser together with amplitude modulators and narrow-band optical filters and converting radar signal to low (envelope) frequencies is considered. Possible characteristics of the receiver are estimated and different modes of its operation are discussed. It is shown that homodyne as well as heterodyne methods for transformation of the spectrum of the input microwave signal into the low frequency region can be used, and linearity of the transformation for these methods is studied. Also, the regime of the optical carrier suppression in modulators is considered. In this case, it is not necessary to use narrow-band optical filters in the scheme. It is shown that, for modern optical elements, signal-to-noise ratio at the output of the system can be 60-70 db and more for a microwave signal with a carrier frequency of tens of gigahertz and a frequency bandwidth of 100 MHz and more.

articleTitle: Timing in GNSS - its importance and challenges
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Heart of satellite based navigation system is timing by precise clocks. In Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS,) mainly consisting of GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and Beiduo, timing plays a vital role also. Coordination of the time scales of all these systems is very important for the optimum utilization of GNSS. It has some stringent requirements. Coordination among different constellations is also a serious issue. This paper details all these aspects.

articleTitle: A CRLH substrate integrated waveguide leaky wave antenna based on Hilbert slot
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of leaky wave antenna based on composite right/left handed (CRLH) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). The design uses the space filling property of Hilbert fractal slot to realize the CRLH response. The slot dimensions are designed in such a way that both the left hand and right hand band operate well below the waveguide cut off frequency which provide a greater level of miniaturization. The main lobe direction of the radiation pattern can be steered from backward to forward direction with a change in frequency. Simulation results for both the input reflection coefficient and radiation patterns are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Conductor-backed coplanar waveguide to microstrip transition on BCB polymer thin film with bandwidth over 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A conductor-backed coplanar waveguide to microstrip via-hole less transition realized on a commercial BCB (Benzocyclobutene) polymer thin film is studied in this paper. By using thin substrates with a low-permittivity, the achieved experimental bandwidth covers the frequency band from 1 GHz to 69 GHz. This transition, using electromagnetic coupling between the bottom and top ground planes, is very useful and requested in component packaging, on-wafer measurements of microstrip based monolithic microwave integrated circuit and for interconnections in hybrid circuits including both microstrip and coplanar structures.

articleTitle: Analysis and mitigation of Raman cross talk in WDM TDM system using partial response coding and Raman pump
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, we analyzed the effects of partial response coding (balance duobinary and dicode coding) in the presence of nonlinear effects. By simulation, we find that the balance duobinary coding is more affected by stimulus Raman scattering (SRS) by an amount of 0.5 dB as compare to dicode coding. So, dicode coding comparatively more tolerance to Raman cross talk in the video Overlay Passive Optical Network (PON). Further in this system 8.3 dB amplification is done by using Raman pump for the data signal to compensate the SRS effect and fiber loss for improving the performance of PON Network.

articleTitle: Design of wire based single/dual/triple band polarization insensitive metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, design, fabrication and measurement of single/dual/triple band absorber based on wire structure is presented. The absorber consists of one/two/three metallic wires for single/dual/triple band absorption. These metallic wires are printed on lossy FR4 sheet backed with metallic plate. The resonant frequency is tuned by changing metallic wire length. The proposed absorbers are polarization insensitive due to four fold rotational symmetry in the design.

articleTitle: Steady state analysis of Tin incorporated Group IV alloy based transistor laser
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper we present a steady state analysis of Si-i<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.12</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.73</sub>Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub>/Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.11</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.73</sub>Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.14</sub> transistor laser (TL) with strain-balanced Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</sub>Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub> single quantum well (QW) in the base. Coupled rate equations in the QW region is used to obtain threshold base current density, steady state electron and photon densities. We find that the nature of variation of threshold base current density, steady state electron and photon density in QW region with electron capture life time is same as in III-V TL. The analysis is helpful for designing the Tin incorporated Group IV alloy based TL.

articleTitle: A modified circular disk patch rectenna for 5.8 GHz HIPERLAN and IEEE 802.11/Wi-Fi applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper describes a rectenna system for HIPERLAN and IEEE 802.11/Wi-Fi applications at 5.8 GHz. The proposed structure uses a modified circular disk patch antenna to collect the electromagnetic energy, a low pass filter for suppressing high order harmonics, a matching circuit to establish matching between the antenna and the rectifier, and a half wave rectifier to convert RF to DC. The antenna resonates at three frequencies (5.8 GHz, 11.6 GHz and 13.2 GHz) and low pass filter cornered around 5.8 GHz removes the other two higher frequency component. For rectification purpose, a Schottky diode rectifier is characterized at 5.8 GHz and the proposed antenna structure is matched with it. The output DC voltage and overall efficiency are respectively higher than 116 mV and 67% at 1 mW/cm2 input power for a 2kΩ resistive load.

articleTitle: High speed fiber-optic systems for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Fiber-optic techniques are very useful for Radar Applications. In this presentation a review of various opto-microwave techniques for radar applications will be given. Later we consider the analysis of Wavelength Division Multiplexed (WDM) networks for distribution of signals in a phased array Radar system. This also includes additional signal conditioning circuitry (electrical) for power equalization This work brings out different optical techniques to equalize this power levels. The techniques are classified as source or detector side equalization methods. The work is supported with modeling and experimental results highlighting their relative advantages and perceived limitations.

articleTitle: Multi-layer Slow-Wave Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Here in this paper a compact Slow-Wave Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SW-SIW) is presented. The scale reduction is done using the Half-Mode SIW method which reduce the lateral dimension of the SIW into the half, along with the three layer Slow-Wave SIW method presented in a previous research paper. Combining these two methods show that the overall scale of the SIW is significantly reduced without affecting the scattering parameters and phase constant, main parameters of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Temperature dependent etching of Gallium Nitride layers grown by PA -MBE
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Future of microwave, power and photonics industry is focused on GaN due to its extraordinary material properties such as wide and direct band gap, large thermal and chemical stability, high breakdown voltage, high saturation velocity. Formation of devices for these applications requires a material selective etching which is performed via wet-etching process. In this paper, temperature dependent etching properties of GaN have been revealed. Molten KOH has been employed as an etchant, to etch 2 µm MBE grown GaN layer on Silicon (111). To verify temperature dependence of GaN etching, etching has been performed at a fixed concentration and etching time. Optimum temperature to etch GaN completely has been determined from Arrhenius plot of etch rate vs temperature. Etch depth has been determined from AFM, whereas, morphology has been confirmed using SEM.

articleTitle: Design of compact meandered dual mode wideband microstrip bandpass filter using tuning stubs
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a new compact meandered dual mode wideband microstrip bandpass filter design using tuning stubs is proposed. Proposed filter is constructed by using bandstop filter with directly connected orthogonal feed lines. The tuning stubs which are of quarter wavelength, located at the opposite sides of input and output sides create a passband within a wide stopband. Perturbation patch located at orthogonal corner with respect to the input and output feed lines excite dual degenerate modes. These dual degenerate modes are responsible for creating two transmission zeros on both upper and lower side of the passband thereby improving the selectivity of the filter. The designed filter which is simulated shows a very low insertion loss of 0.6 dB and return loss level of 11 dB at a center frequency of 4.1 GHz. The fractional bandwidth (FBW) is 49%. Proposed filter achieves a nearly 10% surface area reduction compared to the square loop operating with the same perimeter of the structure.

articleTitle: Designing multiband metamaterial loaded microstrip patch antenna for SAR applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the design of metamaterial (MTM) microstrip patch antennas (MPA) for multiband and wide band applications. The MTM unit cell S-shape loaded reactive impedance surface (S-RIS) is analyzed for square and triangular shape patch antennas. The array of S-RIS unit cell formed metasurface for microstrip patch antenna. It is observed that triangular shape patch gives high bandwidth of 2GHz with directive gain of 5.53dBi while a square shape provide resonance at two frequencies.

articleTitle: CPW-fed Tri-band monopole antenna for wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A Novel and Simple T-shape coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed monopole antenna with filter properties is presented. The proposed monopole antenna consists of a rectangular patch with microstrip resonator has been designed. A coupling structure having a closed loop step-impedance resonator embedded with an open uniform resonator is capable of generating Tri-band monopole antenna. The proposed antenna was designed to operate at three resonating frequencies 2.4, 3.5 and 5 GHz, which covers a frequency bands from (2.37-2.48.GHz), (3.5-3.63GHz), (4.64-5.41GHz) respectively. The tri-band filtering antenna shows monopole-like radiation pattern and gain over the operating bands have been obtained.

articleTitle: Light switching of resistance of LBMO/ZnO hetero p-n junction
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: La(Sr)MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and La(Ba)MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (LBMO) are fabricated on ZnO for novel p-n junction sensitive to UV light. In-plane orientational growths are clarified. LBMO/ZnO shows huge light amplification of current which indicates phase-related resistive change in LBMO by light.

articleTitle: The suitability of normal SOI nanowaveguides for terahertz pulse train generation
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We numerically study the modulational instability (MI) gain at low input powers in a normal silicon-on-insulator (SOI) nanowaveguide. We find that, taking free carrier (FC)-effects in the MI gain analysis made the modulation unstable, due to an additional interaction of free carrier-induced dispersion and nonlinearity and hence made the normal SOI nanowaveguide suitable for nonlinear devices like terahertz pulse train generation, super continuum generation and wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: Optical synchronization of microwave signals in an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A single loop optoelectronic oscillator is synchronized in the optical domain by an external microwave signal. The system equation of such an oscillator has been derived. Normalized output voltage and frequency are calculated and the steady state output voltage as a function of time is studied. Theoretical results are presented in this short communication.

articleTitle: Minimizing coupling losses between bend and straight waveguides
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In photonics integrated circuits two straight waveguide are required to be connected by a bend waveguide incurring coupling losses. In this paper such coupling losses are optimized by the analyzing the bend waveguide by Multiple Scale Method (MSM). The axial shift in electric field is estimated and coupling losses are optimized by introducing offset between straight and bend waveguide.

articleTitle: A Raspberry Pi-based field-deployable tunable diode laser spectroscopy system for the detection of CO2 at 2003.5 nm
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This work reports a real-time, non-invasive, compact and field deployable CO2 sensor using tunable diode laser spectroscopy (TDLAS). Direct detection and 2f-WMS was used to measure the gas parameters utilizing a low power vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) emitting across 2003.5nm where CO2 has a strong absorption line. A Raspberry Pi microcontroller along with a serial analog-to-digital (ADC) convertor was used for data acquisition and processing to make the system compact and field deployable.

articleTitle: Design of shunt-series type slot coupler at X-band
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Present paper describes the analysis procedure of cross-guide waveguide broad wall slot to work as a coupler at X-band. Design has been carried out over the modification of standard Moreno cross-guide coupler for an investigation of power coupling with different slot parameters. Design optimization at X-band has been carried out by taking one slot as variable and contribution of field on the other slot has been observed. Analytical expression for couplers has been deduced to obtain optimized design analytically and complied with simulation result.

articleTitle: On a revisit to Reflex Klystron
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Reflex Klystron Oscillator has been studied again to explore the effects of considering bunching parameter X greater than one. It is observed that as X exceeds unity, the relation between the departure time and the arrival time of the bunched electrons becomes as multivalued function and the Fourier component of the beam current comprises not only the in phase term but also quadrature terms and the equivalent circuit consists of linear negative conductance as well as a non linear reactive part.

articleTitle: Investigations on the optical transitions and linewidth of as-grown III–V quantum dot systems
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper presents the impact of some fundamental parameters on the Gaussian nature of absorption spectra of InxGa1−xAs/GaAs and InxGa1−xN/GaN as-grown quantum dots systems having inhomogeneous indium and size distribution. A analytical expression has also been proposed to evaluate the linewidth of the spectra.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation in fluoride Photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Numerical simulation of supercontinuum generation (SCG) in fluoride based Photonic crystal fiber (PCF) is analyzed using the generalized nonlinear Schrodinger equation and split step Fourier method. Fluoride PCF gives a significant bandwidth enhancement of the SCG as compared to silica based PCF with comparable linear and nonlinear parameters.

articleTitle: Study of polarization resolved absorption in anisotropic quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, we study the polarization sensitive absorption in anisotropic InGaAs/GaAs quantum dot for bound to bound transitions of holes in valence band. It is found that the absorption coefficient for the transitions under consideration are sensitive to in-plane polarization of light due to shape anisotropy of the quantum dot. The response wavelength for different aspect ratio (Radius/height) of quantum dot are found in the range of mid and far-infrared region which are suitable for THz applications.

articleTitle: Ge-content dependent efficiency of Si1−xGex nanorod solar cell with pyramid structure
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper efficiency of Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> based radial p-n junction nanorod array solar cell with pyramidal structure is determined theoretically and its variation is for different Ge-content. A nonlinear variation of overall efficiency of SiGe solar cell with Ge-content (x) is obtained. Efficiency increases with increase in x.

articleTitle: Elastic properties of zincblende III-nitrides: A first-principles study
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have performed first-principle calculations to calculate elastic stiffness constants (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</sub>) and bulk modulus (B) of AlN, GaN and InN semiconductors in the zinc blende structure. These properties are calculated using an ab initio pseudo potential method based on density functional theory (DFT) with the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) for the exchange-correlation functional. The Calculated values are in fair agreement with the values reported by earlier workers.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of wire based bandwidth enhanced metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We present the design and fabrication of a bandwidth enhanced metamaterial absorber, based on multiple wires printed on metal backed lossy dielectric substrate. The proposed structure is fabricated using screen printing technique. In the proposed structure, broadband absorption is achieved by overlapping the absorption peaks of individual wires. Results show that bandwidth of proposed absorber corresponding to 10dB return loss, is 0.5 GHz. The simulated bandwidth of proposed absorber is independent of the variation in incidence angle from 0 to 30°.

articleTitle: Effect of alloy composition on the gain performance of a Si/Ge1−ySny avalanche photodiode
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have investigated the effects of alloy composition (y) on gain of a Ge1-ySny heterostructure avalanche photodiodes (APDs). The band-offsets become a function of alloy composition and affect the carrier confinement at heterointerfaces. The photocurrent is computed using the composition dependent parameters and, hence, the effect of alloy composition on gain of the APDs have been investigated.

articleTitle: Heterojunction detectors from UV to IR
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Heterojunction detectors used as free-carrier and intervalence band detectors for a wide wavelength region are presented. Using a well-studied III-V system of GaAs/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>As to cover a wide wavelength range from UV to far-infrared (THz) is an important development in detector technology. Using the intervalence band (heavy hole, light hole and split off) transitions for high operating temperature detection of mid Infrared radiation is discussed. A promising new way to extend the detection wavelength threshold beyond the standard threshold connected with the energy gap in a GaAs/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>As system is also presented.

articleTitle: Dual band stub loaded microstrip reflectarray antenna with microstrip antenna feed
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A dual-band stub-loaded microstrip reflectarray antenna with microstrip antenna feed is proposed. The 1 × 3, 3 × 1 and plus-shaped reflect-arrays have been studied. A parametric study for varying distances between feed patch and the array has also been done. In dual bands, an optimum gain of more than 8 dBi is obtained in plus shaped array configuration.

articleTitle: Design of a tunable MSM photodetector for photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and fabrication of an integrated tunable MSM PD based on Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) that is fabricated on Si and InP. Tuning is achieved by thermally controlling the bandgap of the semiconductor using a Nickel Chromium (NiCr) microheater which is collocated on the opposite side of the PD substrate.

articleTitle: Study of an electro-optic polymers leaky waveguide deflector and its microwave access across a GCPW to CMS transition for realizing a 40 GSPS AOADC
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper addresses both microwave and optical design of an electro-optic (E-O) polymer leaky waveguide deflector. The designed optical deflector should allow realizing an all-optical analog-to-digital converter (AOADC) operating over 44 giga-samples-per-second (GSPS) with a resolution of 6.5 bits and power consumption of only 4W. In order to make microwave access compatible with the waveguide topology, via-holes less transition from grounded coplanar line to coupled microstrip line (GCPW-CMS) is proposed and realized, with a measured bandwidth of over 35 GHz.

articleTitle: Microwave frequency estimation with high accuracy based on Mach-Zehnder Modulator and Phase Modulator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A technique for microwave frequency estimation with high accuracy based on Mach-Zehnder Modulator and Phase Modulator is proposed and demonstrated. In this proposed technique three dispersive fibers and two wavelengths are used to build power comparison factor. Wavelengths used are extracted from sidebands of MZM and then phase modulated with unknown frequency. Modulated signal is then passed through three stages of dispersive fiber followed by photo-diode. Received power from each photo-diode and its power comparison factors are utilized to estimate unknown frequency in the range of 2 - 20 GHz with maximum error of ±0.1GHz.

articleTitle: Effect of finger spacing on the gain of a silicon avalanche photodetector compatible with CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We present a theoretical study of the gain of a CMOS compatible thin submicron Si-CMOS p-i-n avalanche photodetector (APD) suitable for high-speed, low-voltage operation. A 2-D model is used to estimate the avalanche build-up of carriers in the depleted region considering the dead-space effect. The model is also considered the effects of diffusion of carriers from the substrate region. The results on the gain are shown as a function of finger spacing and bias.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of multilayer triangular microstrip patch antenna with FSS screen
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of truncated equilateral triangular microstrip antenna designed for circular polarization. The antennas are labeled as (a) Antenna Type1; truncated tip triangular patch antenna with parasitic element and air gap and (b) Antenna Type2; truncated tip triangular patch antenna with parasitic element, air gap and FSS screen. The simulated impedance bandwidth of the antenna type1 is about 287.8MHz from 3.52 to 3.81GHz; the 3dB axial ratio (simulated) bandwidth is about 56.6MHz from 3.63 to 3.69GHz. Furthermore, a frequency selective surface (FSS) is used in antenna type2, the impedance bandwidth can be further increased to 289MHz (3.53GHz-3.82GHz), and the 3-dB AR-bandwidth is greatly enhanced from 56.6 to 169.1MHz.

articleTitle: Zeroth-order resonating circular patch antenna with triangular stub for WLAN
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a zeroth-order resonating circular patch antenna with triangular stub is proposed. The proposed antenna has an electrical size of 0.23λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.13λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.01λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with an impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB) of 21.4% (resonating frequency 2.8 GHz). Circuit values of proposed equivalent circuit have been extracted using advanced design system to plot dispersion diagram which shows zeroth order resonance. The proposed metamaterial antenna shows good radiation characteristics with a peak gain of 1.44 dBi and radiation efficiency of 94.8% at 2.8 GHz. The antenna structure shows monopole-type radiation patterns in xz-plane and dipolar-type radiation pattern in yz-plane with very low cross polarization throughout the working band.

articleTitle: The new generation of remote sensors based on the integration of optics and electronics
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The cross-fertilization between photonic and microwave systems is setting new paradigms in radio sensor technologies, providing improved performance and new applications, and allowing for an integration of radio and optics sensors with strong benefits in monitoring and safety applications. Radio sensors as radars are evolving toward multiband multifunctional systems that are putting electronic technologies under pressure. Thanks to its intrinsic high stability, ultra-wide bandwidth, low loss propagation, EMI insensitivity, and high frequency of the optical carrier, photonics can be exploited for facing these new requirements. Photonics can find application in: generation of very stable multiband radiofrequency (RF) sources, very precise and wideband RF signal detection and digitization, wideband beam steering of RF signals in phased array antennas, realization of tunable RF filters, radio over fiber for easier antenna remotization. Moreover, photonics can also be exploited for integrating optical sensors that exhibit complementary features compared to photonics-based RF sensors, in order to improve the awareness of the scene under observation. This integration is based on the partial sharing of the optical hardware, allowing for heterogeneous networks of coherent sensors as well as reduction of power budget and complexity. Finally, on-chip implementations allow for a further reduction of power consumption and footprint.

articleTitle: Wideband microstrip bandpass filter using stub-loaded resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article, a wideband bandpass filter (BPF) using half-wavelength resonator tapped in the middle with loaded stub is presented. The proposed filter has 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 75% with a very sharp cutoff due to two transmission zeros at lower and upper stop-bands. It has low passband insertion-loss with good return-loss characteristics.

articleTitle: Compact CPW-fed ZOR antenna for WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact zeroth-order resonating (ZOR) metamaterial antenna with coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed is presented. The proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 19.82% centered at 3.33 GHz. The proposed structure having smaller electrical size 0.288 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.186 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.018 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free space wavelength at ZOR mode (at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 3.33 GHz). In addition, antenna offers peak gain of 2.41 dB with radiation efficiency of 95.88% at ZOR frequency. It offers excellent omni-directional radiation pattern in yz-plane and dipolar-type radiation pattern in xz-plane. In order to verify the metamaterial behavior, dispersion diagram has been plotted according to the extracted circuit parameters. The proposed antenna can be suitable to be used for WiMAX (3.3-3.6 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of a FSO link under different rain conditions
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Attenuation due to different weather conditions plays a significant role in the performance of the Free Space Optical Communication (FSO). Here, in this paper, we have analyzed the effect of rain on the performance of the FSO Link. We have calculated the link margin for different rain intensity and then experimentally validate the effect of rain on FSO link in term of frame loss.

articleTitle: Photonic Crystal based sensor for small forces
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A Photonic Crystal ring resonator based force sensor is proposed. The device consists of Photonic crystal slab integrated on top of a 220nm thick silicon cantilever and is capable of sensing forces as small as 10nN. The sensitivity is derived as 8.33nN for a wavelength resolution of 0.1nm with a high quality factor of 16000.

articleTitle: Solutions of low-index and high-index contrast optical waveguide by using full-vectorial FEM
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: For any photonic device simulation, accuracy of numerical solution not only depends on methods being used but also on the discretization parameters used in the numerical methods. As solution accuracy may also depend on index contrast used in such photonic devices, the characteristics of a low-index contrast Germanium (Ge) doped Silica and a high-index contrast Silicon (Si) Nanowire Waveguides are analyzed, evaluated and benchmarked. The advantages of using infinite element to deal with boundary condition problem are also presented.

articleTitle: Investigations of plasmonic devices and thermal emission at sub-λ scale using NSOM microscopy
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Infrared near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM) has been used to investigate surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) which are generated on an integrated device by means of a semi-conductor laser. Devices which realize a slit-doublet experiment with SPPs have been investigated. Using NSOM imaging, we demonstrate in situ generation of SPPs with quantum cascade lasers at λ=7.5 μm and with laser diodes at λ=1.3 μm. Using thermal radiation scanning optical microscopy (TRSTM), we measure the infrared thermal emission of a sample, which is scattered in the near-field by means of a tip. We have recorded images and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of the near-field thermal emission of materials which support surface polaritons. We show that the TRSTM probes both the spatial and frequency dependence of the electromagnetic local density of states (EM-LDOS). The modes of SPPs confined on metallic patterns are observed with TRSTM imaging. At the surface of materials supporting surface phonon polaritons, the measured near-field thermal emission spectra are quasi-monochromatic, in striking contrast with blackbody-like far-field thermal emission. TRSTM combined with FTIR spectroscopy is a promising method for infrared spectroscopy with nanoscale resolution, i.e. well beyond the diffraction limit.

articleTitle: Real time monitoring of fringe formation inside LDA measuring volume
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this communication we have developed a technique for monitoring the fringe formation inside LDA measuring volume which allows beam quality, alignment and fringe uniformity to be evaluated in real time. For qualitative as well as quantitative analysis of fringes formed at measurement volume, FESEM analysis has also been performed.

articleTitle: Effect of cladding parameters on supercontinuum generation in water core photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The effect of cladding parameters such as air hole size and pitch, on supercontinuum generation in water core photonic crystal fiber is studied numerically. The influence of cladding parameters on the supercontinuum generation is confirmed in water core photonic crystal fiber which exhibit reorientational characteristics of molecules. Variation in the rate of dispersion as a function of airhole size is found to be the reason for modifications of pulse propagation characteristics in the core.

articleTitle: High performance optical comb filter using full duty cycle based periodically chirped- sampled fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel design of optical comb filter using the effect of periodic chirp and full duty cycle sampling in sampled fiber Bragg grating is proposed and numerically demonstrated. The spectral Talbot phenomenon is realized in the proposed periodically chirped Gaussian-sampled fiber Bragg grating (PC-GSFBG). The channel counts of the filter can be controlled either or both by using FWHM and chirp coefficient. The lesser index modulation can be used to improve channel spacing.

articleTitle: Tri-band dual segment ring dielectric resonator antenna for WiMAX/ WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, tri band dual segment ring dielectric resonator antenna with partial ground plane is presented. Proposed ring shape DRA is excited by modified microstrip line. Two different modes i.e. TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</sub> and HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> are generated in ring DRA at 3.45 GHz and 5.41 GHz respectively. The proposed design operates in three different frequency bands i.e. 2.17 - 2.46 GHz; 3.17-4 GHz; 5-6.5 GHz with the fractional bandwidth of 10.8%; 23.15% and 26.08% respectively. Proposed antenna is able to cover three frequency bands for different wireless applications (WLAN (2.4/5.2/5.8 GHz) and WiMAX (3.5/5.5 GHz) bands). Proposed design has been analyzed, optimized using Ansoft HFSS simulation software. Final simulated results have also been verified using CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Oscillator strength and absorption cross-section of core-shell cubic quantum dot for intraband transition
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, oscillator strength and absorption cross-section of core-shell quantum dot (CSQD) with cubic geometry is computed for both normal and inverted structures. Intraband transitions between lowest three quantum states are considered to study optical properties along with the variation of structural parameters and incident radiation. Kane-type band nonparabolicity of first order is taken into account to study the shift of the oscillator strength and absorption cross-section than that obtained for parabolic overestimation. Result shows that both the properties decreases with increase of device dimension, and the change is more significant for inverted CSQD structure. Higher absorption cross-section is found for transition between lowest two states, and also when calculated for nonparabolic dispersion relation. Result plays significant role in designing CSQD based optical emitter/detector in higher wavelength range.

articleTitle: Barkhausen model of Reflex Klystron Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Reflex Klystron is an oscillator commonly classified under the categories of differential negative conductance oscillators, like Tetrode Oscillator, Gunn Oscillators etc., whereas the Barkhausen oscillator is categorized under the positive feedback system. With the help of physics positive feedback nature of Reflex Klystron, the growth of oscillation leading to its spectral purification and the effect of transit time delay are discussed here. The dependence of Pole-location, Pole-movement, Starting voltage and Jump-phenomenon, hitherto unknown, on mode number has been given.

articleTitle: Image series analysis of broadwall longitudinal slot coupler between parallel waveguides
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A longitudinal coupling slot between parallel rectangular waveguides has been analysed by considering the infinite set of its images in waveguide walls. The internal admittance required for matching the tangential magnetic field is derived using the recently developed closed form point dipole and double dipole approximations alongwith Shanks' transformation for evaluating the mutual admittances between images. The proposed general technique applicable for arbitrarily inclined slots is demonstrated using longitudinal broadwall slot coupler in parallel waveguides and shows good agreement with results from other techniques and experiment.

articleTitle: Finite difference approach for self-consistent solution in strained and strain balanced SiGe/GeSn quantum well
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, quantum mechanical characteristic of strained and strain balanced SiGe/GeSn quantum wells is studied. Eigen energies for Γ valley conduction band, heavy hole band and light hole band are obtained from the self consistent solution of coupled Schrödinger and Poisson equations by finite difference method for both strained and strain balanced quantum wells. A larger splitting of heavy hole band and light hole band in strain balanced quantum well is observed than that of strained quantum well.

articleTitle: Realization of 4 bit optical logic shifter circuit using 4×1 multiplexer
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article presents the 4×1 multiplexer (MUX) by using two GaAs-AlGaAs based optical micro ring resonator (OMRR). The proposed structure of 4×1 MUX is further used as 4 bit optical logic shifter circuit. These models are exploiting the non-linear property of OMRR which enables it to act as an optical switch. The performance of 4 bit logic shifter circuit is analyzed and simulated by using Z-domain modeling in Matlab.

articleTitle: Challenges and innovations in modern antenna technology
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper is aimed to address specific new techniques, which have been developed in the recent years and find potential applications. They basically include printed as well as dielectric resonator antennas and the technique employs deliberately created defects on the ground plane, commonly termed as ‘defected ground structure’ or more popularly ‘DGS’. Over 1200 technical papers, 3 book chapters, and several granted patents produced in the span of last one decade indicate the strength and applicability of the DGS techniques. Fundamental concepts to state of the art innovations will be addressed indicating their possible applications in different fields.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigations on the fast and mixed wave modes for plasma-filled gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The effect of a cold plasma column inside a gyrotron amplifier on a fast wave mode and a mixed wave mode was worked out. The linear dispersion relation was derived with the Vlasov-Maxwell's equation for the hollow and thin electron beam. The effects of the beam location, electron beam parameters and azimuthal harmonic number on the growth rate for both the fast and mixed wave modes were carried out. It is shown that the growth rate and bandwidth of the mixed wave mode is larger than that it is for the fast wave mode.

articleTitle: A new dual loop optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This correspondence reports a new dual loop optoelectronic oscillator (DLOEO). The DLOEO consists of an injection locked oscillator instead of an RF band pass filter(BPF). In addition to this an external sync signal is injected to the system and locking phenomena of the synchronized system is observed.

articleTitle: Use of particle swarm optimization to obtain designing parameters from data set of frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: To get designing parameters of a frequency selective surface is very difficult and time consuming. This work suggests a method where different designing parameters with its respective resulting factors are kept in a data set from where accurate designing factors can be found for a desired frequency. Particle swarm optimization technique is suggested for proper searching. This algorithm can search efficiently and find approximate value of the desired parameters if the accurate one is not present in the data set. This paper deals with a data set. It includes different periodicities in a two dimensional array of circular patch type frequency selective surfaces and the resonating frequencies of the structures. Particle swarm optimization program efficiently searches from this data set and shows periodicity for a desired frequency.

articleTitle: A compact circularly polarized broadband microstrip slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a broadband circularly polarized microstrip slot antenna fed by a coplanar waveguide. The broadband circular polarization is achieved by projecting an `□' shaped metallic strip from the ground plane towards the center of the slot. Simulated results show an impedance bandwidth of 32.27%, AR bandwidth of 9.1% and gain of 4.28 dBi. Measured results of fabricated prototype shows 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 28.91%.
